text:
anya: Heads up — noticed a backlog of recompute jobs in EU shard, priority signals look skewed after last night's ingest spike.

sanjay: saw that. queue length spiked around 02:12 UTC, a bunch of small tenants flooded the high-priority lane.

mike: are those the new console priority tags? I thought the smoothing was supposed to prevent thrash.

beth: It is supposed to, but we changed the default smoothing factor to 0.0 in the last deploy for latency experiments. That made recent bursts fully surface.

anya: ahh. that explains it. propose: run a dry-run recompute that applies smoothing=0.3 and compares slot allocation delta.

sanjay: +1. also ensure routing respects tenant fair-share: when slots < 200, cap any tenant at 5% by default.

mike: can we simulate? quick script to apply smoothing: ```python
def smooth(old, mean, alpha=0.3):
    return old*(1-alpha) + mean*alpha
```
run against the last 24h weight vector.

beth: i'll spin a staging backfill with the new smoothing and route it to slice-3 only. planning ~50 tenants, low-cost window.

ops-bot: Triggered backfill job: job_id=bf-20260401-77 status=queued route=slice-3 smoothing=0.3

anya: console UX note: the backfill estimate currently shows bytes and wall-time. PMs interpret it as total compute. we should surface "compute-est" (vCPU*sec or token-est) and a confidence band.

sanjay: agree — i'll take the dashboard piece. add a metric: backfill.compute_token_est and backfill.compute_est_confidence.

mike: API change: we need a per-tenant throttle knob so support can lower priority for noisy tenants without cancelling jobs. small endpoint: POST /v1/backfills/{id}/throttle {tenant_id, rate_pct}. will file.

beth: filed: PLATFORM-3823 (console compute-est + confidence) and INFRA-990 (per-tenant throttle API). link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PLATFORM-3823

anya: staging dry-run checklist: capture token-latency, per-tenant error-rate, queue-hold-time, and percentile work-per-slot. abort if error-rate > 0.5% or 95th token-latency regresses >20%.

sanjay: noted. i'll wire a Grafana snapshot panel and set a temporary alert rule for the dry-run window.

mike: rollout plan: canary 10% slices, monitor 15m. if healthy, 50% for 1h, then full. rollback path: revert smoothing flag and re-route queued jobs to baseline slot allocator.

beth: scheduling canary for 03:30 UTC window to avoid peak. i'll post follow-up with exact tenant list.

anya: tagging @oncall in case we need immediate rollback. please be on standby 03:25-04:00 UTC.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: bf-20260401-77 -> canary window 03:30-04:30 UTC.

mike: thanks team. after canary, let's capture a before/after heatmap of slot utilization to validate smoothing impact.

beth: :thumbsup:

anya: closing loop: if staging looks good i'll convert dry-run config into an adaptive default (alpha=0.25) and ship a console message explaining the change.

sanjay: sounds good. i'll update the dashboard and alert links in the ticket.

mike: LGTM.
